title: Understand computer vision at work · Level 2
slo: Identify what computer vision does and match it to common workplace uses.

exercises.question_text: Inspecting assembly-line products for surface defects is manufacturing defect ___.

parts.text: Inspecting assembly-line products for surface defects is manufacturing defect

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The factory task would be assigned to the wrong use case.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use this term for visual quality checks on manufactured products.

exercises.explanation: Manufacturing defect detection inspects assembly-line products for defects.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces to form a correct statement about segmentation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition of segmentation becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the capability, then state what it divides and why.

exercises.correct_answer: Image segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions for detailed analysis.
exercises.explanation: Segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions for closer analysis.

exercises.question_text: A factory manager sees misaligned parts as products pass a camera and must choose a system feature. What should the system support?

options.rationale: This is correct. Manufacturing vision can inspect moving products for misalignments.
This is incorrect. Scan review concerns medical images, not factory products.
options.better_fit: Radiologist scan review fits X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans.

feedback.instructional: An assembly-line quality issue needs real-time product inspection.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Inventory updates track store shelf stock and placement.
options.better_fit: Shelf inventory updates fit retail shelf monitoring.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would not receive product-quality information.
feedback.instructional: Misalignments are manufacturing defects, not inventory events.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Road-sign recognition supports vehicle navigation.
options.better_fit: Road-sign recognition fits autonomous vehicle vision.

feedback.instructional: Choose inspection features for quality decisions on the line.

exercises.explanation: Correct—real-time inspection can catch misaligned parts.

exercises.question_text: A factory inspector must locate every screw in a product photo and inspect each screw area closely. Which capabilities should the system use? Select all that apply.

options.text: Object detection to locate each screw
options.rationale: This is correct. Detection identifies screws and their locations.

options.text: Image segmentation to inspect object areas
options.rationale: This is correct. Segmentation supports detailed analysis of image areas.
This is incorrect. Creating screws does not inspect the photographed product.
options.better_fit: Image generation fits creating or editing visual content.

feedback.intrinsic: Missing or damaged screws could remain undetected.
feedback.instructional: Use detection for locations and segmentation for detailed areas.

options.text: Retail shelf monitoring to count stock
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Shelf monitoring concerns store inventory, not product-part inspection.
options.better_fit: Retail shelf monitoring fits cameras observing store shelves.

feedback.intrinsic: The product photo would not receive the needed inspection.
feedback.instructional: This decision requires image-analysis capabilities for the screws themselves.

exercises.explanation: Correct—detection locates screws and segmentation supports close inspection.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the tool and scan review becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the capability first, then who it helps, followed by the scan types.

exercises.correct_answer: Computer vision can help radiologists analyze X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans.
exercises.explanation: Computer vision assists radiologists with analysis of medical scans.

exercises.question_text: The AI field that interprets images, videos, and camera feeds is ___.

parts.text: The AI field that interprets images, videos, and camera feeds is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The capability would be named incorrectly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use computer vision for understanding existing visual input.

exercises.question_text: A radiologist has many CT scans to review and wants help finding possible anomalies. Which outcomes should the hospital expect? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Fractures are possible anomalies the system can highlight.
This is correct. Earlier attention to possible anomalies can support diagnosis.
This is incorrect. Inventory updates result from monitoring retail shelves.
options.better_fit: Retail shelf monitoring fits out-of-stock or misplaced products.

feedback.intrinsic: The scan-review need would remain unsupported.
feedback.instructional: CT-scan analysis can highlight anomalies and support radiologists, not store inventory.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Missing-component checks are manufacturing quality control.
options.better_fit: Manufacturing defect detection fits assembly-line inspection.

feedback.intrinsic: The radiologist would not receive anomaly support.
feedback.instructional: Choose outcomes tied to analysis of medical scans.

exercises.explanation: Correct—medical imaging analysis can support anomaly review and early diagnosis.

exercises.question_text: A support app receives customer photos and must identify visible objects before routing each case. Which capability should its designer choose?

options.rationale: This is correct. It can identify objects in the submitted photos.
This is incorrect. It creates images instead of identifying objects in a photo.
options.better_fit: Use image generation when the app must create a new visual from a prompt.

feedback.intrinsic: The submitted photo would remain unanalyzed.
feedback.instructional: The decision requires understanding an existing image, which is computer vision.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Generating video does not inspect a supplied photo.
options.better_fit: Use video generation when creating a video from instructions.

feedback.intrinsic: The visible object would not be identified.
feedback.instructional: Choose a visual-analysis capability for object identification in photos.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. The required evidence is in the customer photo.
options.better_fit: Text-only processing fits a request containing only written information.

feedback.instructional: Choose computer vision when the needed information is in an image.

exercises.explanation: Correct—computer vision can automate object identification in photos.

exercises.question_text: Using cameras to detect out-of-stock products on store shelves is retail shelf ___.

parts.text: Using cameras to detect out-of-stock products on store shelves is retail shelf

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The inventory task would be mislabeled.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use retail shelf monitoring for camera-based store shelf checks.

exercises.explanation: Retail shelf monitoring uses cameras to check stock and placement.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces to form a correct statement about changing road conditions.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The role of visual recognition in road decisions becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with visual recognition, then state that it supports decisions in changing road environments.

exercises.correct_answer: Visual recognition supports decisions in changing road environments.
exercises.explanation: Autonomous vehicle vision uses visual recognition to support decisions as road conditions change.

exercises.question_text: A store manager needs camera alerts when a product is missing from a shelf. What should the manager enable?

options.rationale: This is correct. Shelf monitoring can trigger timely inventory updates.
This is incorrect. Early diagnosis support is a medical imaging outcome.
options.better_fit: Early diagnosis support fits review of medical images for anomalies.

feedback.intrinsic: The missing item might not trigger the required alert.
feedback.instructional: The decision is about shelf availability, which requires inventory updates.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Quality control checks manufactured products for defects.
options.better_fit: Assembly-line quality control fits factory product inspection.

feedback.intrinsic: The empty shelf would remain unaddressed.
feedback.instructional: Store shelves require inventory monitoring, not factory inspection.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Road navigation concerns vehicles and traffic scenes.
options.better_fit: Autonomous vehicle vision fits navigation decisions in changing roads.

feedback.intrinsic: No shelf alert would be configured.
feedback.instructional: Match the capability to a store-inventory decision.

exercises.explanation: Correct—shelf monitoring enables real-time inventory updates.

exercises.question_text: A self-driving vehicle approaches a busy crossing. Which visual information should its safety system recognize? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Pedestrians are essential road users to recognize.
This is correct. Other vehicles affect safe navigation decisions.
This is incorrect. Shelf stock is not crossing-safety information.
options.better_fit: Retail shelf monitoring fits detecting shelf stock issues.

feedback.intrinsic: Critical crossing information could receive less attention.
feedback.instructional: At a crossing, recognize road users and navigation information rather than store inventory.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. CT-scan anomalies are medical imaging evidence.
options.better_fit: Medical imaging analysis fits assisting radiologists with scans.

feedback.intrinsic: The safety system would not focus on the traffic scene.
feedback.instructional: Choose visual information that affects the vehicle's immediate road decision.

exercises.explanation: Correct—pedestrians and other vehicles are critical at a busy crossing.
